title: Mixtures & alligation
examples: How do I find the ratio if I know the total volume?
Can you show me an example using paint colors?
Is there a formula for mixing solutions?

explain.say: Today we are learning about mixing different substances.

items: Mixing involves combining two or more things.
We use ratios to find the correct amounts.
The ratio shows the relative amounts needed.

explain.say: A ratio compares the amounts of different parts.

draw.text: Ratio: Part A to Part B

explain.say: If you mix flour and sugar, the ratio matters.
To find the mixing ratio, divide the amounts.
If you need a solution that is one part acid to two parts water, the ratio is one to two.
In real life, mixing paint colors uses this same ratio concept.

faq.q: How do I simplify the ratio after finding it?
faq.a: You should always simplify the ratio to its lowest whole number terms. For example, a ratio of four to six simplifies to two to three.
asks: What is the simplest form of a ratio?
How do I make the ratio smaller?

faq.q: Does the order of the ratio matter?
faq.a: Yes, the order is very important because it tells you which ingredient is which. If you write flour to sugar, it is different from sugar to flour.
asks: Is the order important in ratios?
Does A:B mean the same as B:A?
Why must I keep the order correct?

faq.q: What if the amounts are given in different units?
faq.a: First, you must convert all measurements into the same unit, like milliliters or grams. You cannot mix units directly.
asks: Can I use liters and cups in the same ratio?
Do I need to convert units first?
What if the units are different?

faq.q: Is alligation only for chemical mixtures?
faq.a: No, you can use ratio concepts for any mixing, such as recipes, paint, or even budgeting proportions. The principle is the same.
asks: Can I use ratios for cooking?
Does this apply to money mixing?

faq.q: When should I use a ratio instead of just dividing?
faq.a: You use a ratio when you need to describe the proportional relationship between two or more parts. Dividing gives you a single resulting number.
asks: When is ratio better than division?
What is the difference between ratio and division?
Do I always divide to find a ratio?

facts: A ratio compares quantities of two or more values.
The components of a ratio must be in the same units.
Ratios can be written using a colon, like A:B, or as a fraction.
Simplifying a ratio means dividing all parts by their greatest common divisor.

quiz.say: A recipe calls for three cups of flour and two cups of milk. What is the ratio of flour to milk?
quiz.why: The ratio is written directly from the given order of ingredients, which is three to two.

wrong.1: This adds the amounts together, which is incorrect for a ratio.
wrong.2: This represents a single fraction, not the proportional comparison needed.
wrong.3: This assumes the amounts are equal, ignoring the stated measurements.

quiz.say: You mix a solution that is 100 milliliters of acid and 200 milliliters of water. What is the simplest ratio of acid to water?
quiz.why: Both amounts are divided by 100, giving the simplest whole number ratio of one to two.

wrong.0: This incorrectly adds the amounts together before forming the ratio.
wrong.2: This is the original ratio, but it is not in its simplest form.
wrong.3: This reverses the order, suggesting the water amount is the first part.

quiz.say: If a mixture needs a ratio of oil to vinegar of 5:3, and you use 15 liters of vinegar, how much oil do you need?
quiz.why: Since three parts equal 15 liters, one part equals five liters. Five parts then equal 25 liters.

wrong.1: This incorrectly assumes that the ratio must be kept at the original numbers.
wrong.2: This only calculates the amount for one part, not the required five parts.
wrong.3: This suggests a direct one-to-one relationship between the parts.
